scoring_justification: Headline quantities are deterministic outputs of a complex finite‑element / ray‑tracing simulation pipeline. Full recompute of the entire pipeline inside the verifier is infeasible, so we compare the agent's reported scalar values against paper‑reported references with tolerances. This is a valid T0 approach per D4.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference gold values for all scored artifacts
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Tables/Fig.8, Fig.9, Eq.8, Eq.20; reference solution solve.sh reproduces the same numbers.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's reported numerical results (GT = 4.03e-5 mm⁻¹, nodes retained = 65.7%, correlation = 0.97, validation peak = 24.0 mm, rms original = 0.552 waves, rms reconstructed = 0.543 waves, relative error = 1.63%).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact values reported in the paper, verified against the reference solver, and used only for comparison against the agent's reproduced output.

outputs.description: Harmonic-mean refractive index gradient magnitude threshold.
Percentage of original refractive index nodes retained and correlation coefficient between original and reconstructed fields.
X-coordinate of the PSF peak from the gradient-index slab ray-tracing validation.
RMS wave aberration of original and reconstructed refractive index fields, and the relative error between them.

output_contract.notes: All output files must be placed under /app/outputs. The finite-element simulation step is not scored directly; only its downstream optical products are verified. The ray-tracing algorithm must be implemented according to the described recursive grid-based method; no external ray-tracing library is assumed.

steps.description: Harmonic-mean threshold GT (mm⁻¹). Compare to paper value 4.03e-05 within ±10% relative.
Nodes retained percent and correlation coefficient. nodes_retained_percent within ±5% absolute of 65.7; correlation_coefficient ≥ 0.95.
PSF peak x-coordinate (mm). Compare to 24.0 mm within ±0.1 mm.

RMS wave aberrations and relative error. rms_original and rms_reconstructed within 10% relative of paper values (0.552, 0.543). relative_error_percent computed from submitted values must be ≤ 5% (lower is better).
